scope: Real account creation, sign-in, sign-out, session persistence, validation, and account isolation.

environment.storage: Isolated temporary SQLite databases with disposable QA accounts

fixes.issue: Signup returned an error after a session write failed, but left the email registered and prevented retrying.
fixes.cause: Account and session writes committed independently.
fixes.change: Create the account and its initial session in one SQLite transaction; set the cookie after commit.
fixes.regression: tests/accounts.test.ts: signup rolls back the account when its initial session cannot be saved
fixes.before: Session INSERT failure returned 500 but left a user row.
fixes.after: Failure returns 500 without a cookie or account row; retry succeeds with a usable session.

fixes.issue: A new account inherited the previous account's unsaved character name, description, and reference photos.
fixes.cause: Sign-out only cleared the user; private form state remained mounted.
fixes.change: Clear account-specific state on identity changes and initialize the next account's own name.
fixes.regression: scripts/account-browser-regressions.js: drafts and reference photos are isolated between accounts
fixes.before: Browser reproduction showed the first account's draft name and photo under the second account.
fixes.after: The second account starts with its own name, empty description, and no photos.

fixes.issue: A delayed collection response from a previous account could render its records under a new account.
fixes.cause: Refresh checked component lifetime without checking whether the authenticated account had changed.
fixes.change: Track an account epoch and ignore stale session, collection, authentication, upload, and action results. Recheck sessions on focus and visibility restoration.
fixes.regression: scripts/account-browser-regressions.js: late collection responses cannot cross account boundaries
fixes.before: A held collection response released after sign-out and signup appeared in the new account's collection.
fixes.after: The old response is ignored; external session invalidation also returns the UI to the empty authentication form.

fixes.issue: A connection failure displayed a raw English browser error.
fixes.cause: Fetch rejections bypassed the API client's user-facing error handling.
fixes.change: Return a Spanish connection-and-retry message while preserving server validation errors.
fixes.regression: tests/creator-api.test.ts: account requests explain a lost connection and allow callers to retry
fixes.before: The actual signup form displayed Failed to fetch.
fixes.after: The production form explains the connection failure and permits retrying.

fixes.issue: An unreadable HTTP 200 response was treated as a successful account request.
fixes.cause: JSON parsing errors were converted to a result object even on successful HTTP status codes.
fixes.change: Reject unreadable or non-object responses rather than returning a successful result.
fixes.regression: tests/creator-api.test.ts: account requests reject unreadable successful responses instead of claiming success
fixes.before: The API client resolved an HTML HTTP 200 response instead of rejecting it.
fixes.after: The production form shows the retry message, stays signed out, and successfully creates the account after the response recovers.

browserRegression.run: Evaluate on /create against an isolated QA server. It creates disposable accounts through the forms and finishes signed in to its first account.

production.name: drafts and reference photos are isolated between accounts
late collection responses cannot cross account boundaries
wrong-password errors allow retrying the existing account

apiChecks: Reject malformed signup bodies, blank and short names, long names, invalid and oversized emails, non-string fields, short passwords, and passwords longer than 128 characters.
Accept boundary names of 2 and 24 characters and passwords of 8 and 128 characters.
Trim names, preserve Unicode names, and trim/lowercase email addresses.
Create a usable HttpOnly SameSite=Lax session without requiring an AI provider.
Return only the public user fields in account/session responses.
Reject case-insensitive duplicate emails without issuing a replacement cookie.
Race three identical signups and create exactly one user and one session.
Return identical wrong-credential errors for existing and missing accounts.
Issue a fresh session token when signing in.
Invalidate the signed-out session without invalidating another account's session.
Reject expired and malformed session cookies.
Keep accounts and sessions usable after a server restart.
Reject cross-site signup requests without creating an account.
Rate-limit excessive signup requests while session and health reads remain available.
Set and clear the Secure HttpOnly cookie consistently for secure deployments.
Roll back account creation when the initial session cannot be persisted, then retry successfully.
browserChecks: Blank signup is blocked by native form validation before an HTTP request.
Real form signup creates the account, signs it in, and opens its workshop.
Passwords are cleared after successful authentication and session cookies are not exposed through document.cookie.
Sign out, create a second account, and verify that draft text and photo previews do not transfer.
Hold an authenticated collection response across sign-out and new signup; verify that its old records do not appear.
Show a wrong-password error, correct the password, and sign into the original account through the real form.
Reload the production page and restore the same authenticated account.
Keep another browser session signed in when the first is signed out.
Invalidate the session outside the component, return focus, and clear the private editor and authentication fields.
Show a duplicate-email error in the actual signup form without authenticating.
At 320 pixels wide, show signup and workshop without horizontal overflow.
Drop the signup fetch, show a readable error, and keep the retry button usable.
Return HTML with status 200, show an error without signing in, then retry against the real server and create the account.
limitations: Production browser checks used localhost with production cookie settings. A public HTTPS domain and reverse proxy were not exercised.
Mobile layout was checked in a browser viewport, not on physical phones.
The delayed-collection regression injects a controlled old-account response to reproduce the asynchronous privacy bug.
